files.text:
# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — build the capability from an empty seed: grading contract (values, not formulas) + openpyxl writing + examples-as-spec + inspect/verify workflow
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md "How the file is graded" (cluster A, ~13 tasks): data_only, no recalc, so write computed literals even for formula/VBA requests. Load the save-workbook with data_only=True to keep existing formula cells' values. Use real types and the first-sheet rule.
  - prompt.md "Write with openpyxl" (cluster B): pandas for reading only. Explains the to_excel row-shift, NA-string and dropped-sheet hazards.
  - prompt.md "Reading the task" (clusters C and D): preview row mapping and "Unnamed" headers; (row label, column header) semantics and matrix axes; existing values are worked examples to reproduce; copy example layouts including their header; verbatim labels; fill colour via fgColor.rgb; float tolerance; always perform the operation (append despite duplicates).
  - task_template.md (new; cluster E): full field framing plus a 5-step procedure (inspect → rule check vs examples → write values → reopen and print the answer range → no-code reply to finish). Replaces "once that file exists, you are done".
- Expected effect and safety: should fix most of cluster A (37378, 46897, 53647, 55049, 56563, 6698, 7902, 8942, 37456, and part of 53383/54144/9569/55979), plus 267-18, 59196, 80-42, 227-40 and 50768 where the inspection catches the layout. All 18 passers already write literal values. The openpyxl preference and the verify step do not change their answers, only add 1-2 rounds.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: pure semantic misreads (43436, 51-12, 48527, 39046) depend on the reader actually honouring the "reproduce existing examples" check. If they still fail, add a worked mini-example of checking a rule against pre-filled cells.
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration: read the new traces for the formula cluster first. If any still write "=...", strengthen the contract. Then look at whether the verify step fires (reopen and print) and whether any passer regressed because of the openpyxl preference.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.750 Δ=+0.300 · fixed={267-18, 37378, 39046, 46897, 53383, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569} · broke={2768, 45635} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.750 Δ=+0.300 -->

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: empty seed → one broad candidate covering all diagnosed clusters at once. The largest lever by far is the grading CONTRACT (values vs formulas), found by reading evaluation.py plus the adapter rather than the traces alone. Result not known at write time.
- Diagnosis method that paid off: diff init vs golden cells for each failing task. This revealed that "wrong logic" failures were often layout/offset errors (pandas round-trip) or ignored example values. That class is invisible from the feedback string alone.
- What to try next: if val rises but the semantic-misread tasks remain, switch lever from KNOWLEDGE bullets to a worked procedure example (a check-against-prefilled-cells snippet) in task_template.md. Watch the round counts for the added verify step.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001 (spreadsheetbench verified probe)
- With an EMPTY seed and no task_template.md, the proposer has to reconstruct the built-in template from adapter source to know what the agent actually sees. Copying the effective default template (and the scorer's comparison rules) into the work dir as a read-only reference would save a large part of the diagnosis.
- rejected.jsonl is referenced by CLAUDE.md, but on iteration 1 it does not exist. Say "may be absent on the first iteration" to avoid a wasted search.
- The golden files are named *_golden.xlsx in the data dir, while the vendored evaluation.py refers to *_answer.xlsx. A one-line note on where the gold files live would help trace-vs-gold diffing.

files.text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Fill this in as you work. It is the human-readable record of HOW this iteration was done and is snapshotted with the candidate, so anyone — and the next iteration via ./prior_iterations/ — can see your reasoning. Be concrete.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A: formula written instead of value | 37378, 46897, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569, 37456 (~13) | Scorer reads data_only=True with no recalc, so an openpyxl-written formula reads back as None. The agent follows "give me a formula/VBA" literally. | KNOWLEDGE (grading contract) | CONTRACT in prompt.md |
| 2 | C: existing target/example values ignored or overwritten | 39046, 48527, 59196, 43436, 54144, 53383, 9569, 51-12 | The agent never reads the pre-filled cells / labels that define the expected output shape | BEHAVIORAL | procedure (task_template.md) + KNOWLEDGE (prompt.md) |
| 3 | B: pandas to_excel round-trip corrupts layout | 39046, 43436, 48527, 50768, 227-40, 80-42 | Header-in-row-1 assumption and iloc offsets shift rows; other sheets are dropped; the matrix axes were misread (50768) | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md: write with openpyxl at explicit coordinates |
| 4 | E: no inspection, no verification, stuck loops | 39046, 43436, 80-42 (+ most of A/C) | "once that file exists, you are done" means writing in round 1-2 and never checking; the same silent code is repeated for 30 rounds | BEHAVIORAL | ordered workflow + verify step in task_template.md |
| 5 | D: specific knowledge gaps | 267-18 (fill color + formula cached value), 80-42 (append despite duplicates), 227-40 (copy example block incl. header), 55979 (verbatim labels) | Missing know-how | KNOWLEDGE | one bullet each in prompt.md |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | CONTRACT | prompt.md "How the file is graded" | States the actual scorer semantics (values only, data_only, no recalc). Formula/VBA requests are answered with computed values. Applies to every task. | Yes: all 18 passers already write literal values |
| A/D (267-18) | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md | Load the save-workbook with data_only=True so existing formula cells keep their values. Transform the cached value when changing a formula cell. | Yes: passers overwrite the target cells anyway |
| B | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md "Write with openpyxl" | Explains the row offset of pandas (iloc i = row i+2), NA-string loss and dropped sheets. Recommends openpyxl cell writes. pandas is still fine for reading. | Yes: phrased as a preference; passers' pandas outputs were correct values anyway |
| C | KNOWLEDGE + BEHAVIORAL | prompt.md "Reading the task" + template step 2 | Existing values/examples are the spec, and the rule must reproduce them. Row/column labels define the cell meaning; check the matrix axes. | Yes: passing tasks have consistent examples, so the check is a no-op |
| D | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md bullets | Fill colour via fgColor.rgb, copy verbatim labels, reproduce the example layout with its header, append even if the rows repeat, float tolerance | Bounded: each bullet only triggers on its situation |
| E | BEHAVIORAL | task_template.md "How to work" | Inspect → rule check → write values → reopen and print the answer range → no-code reply to end. Fits the adapter's VERIFY_TURNS=3 and its no-code-ends-loop rule. | Yes: adds 1-2 rounds; far below the 30-round cap |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- A: 37378 wrote `'=IF(B{row}<>"", COUNTA($B$2:B{row}), "")'` and the feedback says the answer cells hold FORMULAS. The prompt now says a written formula reads back empty and scores zero, so the agent should compute COUNTA in Python and write ints. Checked against evaluation.py:160 (data_only=True) and compare_cell_value (None vs number → False).
- A/D: 267-18. Init G cells are formulas, and the gold G2 is `//` + computed string. The prompt's "transform its cached value and write the literal result" plus the data_only load matches exactly what gold holds.
- B: 50768. `header=None` + iloc wrote values one row off, and the axes were swapped (gold H12='4, 6', F14='1, 3, 5'). The prompt's pandas row-offset rule plus the "(row label, column header) pair … check which axis" bullet targets both errors. The template's step 1 prints the labels around the range.
- C: 39046. The existing column shows per-row counts, gold [2,2,0,2,2]; the agent wrote a total. Template step 2 ("rule must reproduce every existing example value") would reject a total rule. The same applies to 43436 (existing H pattern), 53383 (Matched/Not Matched) and 9569 (AO9 example).
- C: 59196. The header is in row 2. The "Unnamed: n means the real header sits lower" bullet plus the openpyxl inspection targets this.
- D: 80-42. The gold appends from row 4000 despite the duplicates. The "Always carry out the requested operation … even when similar rows already exist" bullet targets this. 227-40: the gold includes the header row; the "reproduce that layout, header row included" bullet targets this. 55979: the gold uses the sheet name 'Supplier_1'; the verbatim-label bullet targets this.
- E: 39046/43436/80-42 repeated identical silent code for up to 30 rounds. The template says "fix the cause rather than re-sending … Print something in every block". The verify step ends with a no-code reply, which the adapter treats as done (adapter.py: `if solution_code: break`).
- Template placeholder contract validated with the adapter's own `_task_template_error(cand_dir)` → None; `.format(...)` renders cleanly.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used (or: "serial fallback because …"): none. The work was serial because the session policy forbids AgentTool/workflows unless the user requests them. Diagnosis was done by dumping all 40 traces, then diffing init vs golden cells for each failing task.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md (which, and what I learned): none exist (first iteration; seed capability empty; no rejected.jsonl).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The values-not-formulas grading contract (the largest cluster; applies to every task).
- The verify-then-no-code-reply ending (matches the adapter's loop semantics).
- The placeholder layout (all six required + {max_turns}) of task_template.md (validated).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- No task-specific rules for individual semantic misreads, such as the exact counting rule in 43436 or 51-12. They are covered only by the generic "reproduce the examples" check, because hardcoding them would be answer-leaking.
- No infra cluster: every rollout had error=None.

---

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate

# Optimize the capability — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED prompt fixes this iteration

{{TARGET_READER}}

{{FOCUS_SUMMARY}}

{{EMPTY_SEED}}

GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `{{CAP_BRIEF}}` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
